heading: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - CLOCK TOWER JURY ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - CLOCK TOWER JURY ROOM - DAY
A circular chamber at the top of a stone tower, walls hung with portraits of long-dead judges.
A great brass clock mechanism ticks behind a glass panel.
Rain beads on the narrow windows.
A long oak table, six empty water glasses.
JUDGE AUGUSTINE FAIRWEATHER, sixties, silver-haired and courtly in his robes, pours tea from a thermos.
Across from him sits ATTORNEY ROSALIND MACALLISTER, forties, sharp-suited, with a folder held flat in front of her like a shield.
Beside her, ATTORNEY THADDEUS PRUITT, fifties, rumpled, taps a pencil in rhythm with the clock.
Sugar, Miss Macallister?
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: No, thank you, Your Honor.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: Mr. Pruitt?
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: Two. Please.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: I like these hours before the jury comes up. A man gets to remember he's old.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: You're not old, Judge.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: That's what a defence attorney says.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: We're not here to discuss your age, Judge. We're here about the motion.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: Ah, yes. The motion.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: He sips.
Sets down the cup.
Smiles at them both with enormous warmth.
Your Honor, my client has been very patient.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Your client has been very patient for eleven months. Mine has been waiting for six years.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: Rosalind, with respect-
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Thaddeus, with none.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: Children. Children.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: He holds up a hand.
The clock behind the glass chimes the half hour and everything in the room trembles with it.
I have read both briefs. Twice. Once in the afternoon and once at three in the morning, because that's when a man reads honestly.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: And?
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: And I find they're not so different as they pretend to be.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: That's... encouraging.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Isn't it.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: Footsteps on the stair.
The door swings open and a young woman enters, breathless, a stack of documents hugged to her chest.
CLERK PRISCILLA NAKASHIMA, twenty-six, wears a plain grey suit and an expression of dread.
Your Honor. Forgive me. This just came from the records office.
units.name: PRISCILLA

units.text: Thank you, Miss Nakashima. Put it here.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: She sets the stack in front of him.
He opens the top envelope.
Reads.
His smile does not move, but something behind it does.
Judge?
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: It seems the original deed was never recorded.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: What?
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: That's impossible. I filed it myself.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: You filed a copy, Miss Macallister. The original was delivered to this office in 1987 and signed for by a clerk who is now deceased.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: It was misfiled. Under the wrong township.
units.name: PRISCILLA

units.text: Which means the transfer-
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Never legally occurred.
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: Which means, if I'm reading this right, that neither of your clients owns the property in question.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: Silence.
The clock ticks.
Pruitt sits back down, slowly, as if the chair might break.
Macallister stares at the judge.
Then who does?
units.name: MACALLISTER

units.text: The county.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: He picks up his tea.
Sips it.
Looks at the portraits on the wall, the long line of dead men in black.
I suggest we all have a very long think, and then a very short settlement.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER

units.text: Shall I fetch the jury, Your Honor?
units.name: PRISCILLA

units.text: No, my dear. I think the jury can go home.
units.name: FAIRWEATHER
